best_adapter.mechanism: --no-policy-loss flag: only ECHO auxiliary loss runs, no GRPO policy gradient. Avoids the verbosity / clean-class-collapse pathology that hurt all 13+ policy-gradient iters.

runner_up.note: Statistically tied with iter 25. Earlier lucky GRPO result. Less interpretable mechanism.

key_finding: GRPO's policy gradient is the primary mechanism of harm on saturated-baseline capabilities (>=0.94 base composite). Removing it (--no-policy-loss, ECHO-only) ties or beats every other recipe. The drift class improved from 0.975 to 1.000 with no other class regressed materially.
recommendation: Use iter 25's adapter, OR just use the base model (statistically equivalent on composite). For future capabilities at saturation, default to --no-policy-loss or pivot to OPD.
